was: Soil is strong because its grains press on each other, and water pressure in the gaps pushes them apart.
now: Soil holds as well as its grains press on one another, and water in the gaps, pushing or pulling, changes that press.
why: Water pressure acts equally on every grain round a gap; it takes part of the load the grains carry between them rather than pushing them apart.

was: With nothing pressing the grains together, friction between them vanishes
now: Grains that hardly press can hardly grip
why: The grains still touch and still press a little; their grip falls with the press, toward zero, rather than vanishing outright.
